page: Microsoft Azure D128lds_v7 is an x86_64 instance powered by the Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running under Microsoft Hyper-V. The server allocates 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores, operating with two hardware threads per core at clock frequencies up to 4.2 GHz. Its cache architecture features 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 480 MB L3 cache pool. System memory totals 256 GB, resulting in an allocation ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance is not equipped with discrete accelerators but bundles 7559 GB of fast local NVMe SSD scratch storage alongside support for external Premium Storage.

The platform leverages Intel instruction set capabilities, including AVX-512, AMX Tile and Int8, VAES, and SHA-NI, which translate to top-tier multi-threaded compute performance. Multi-core synthetic evaluations place its compute throughput in the top ten percent, demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 145,373.21 and a PassMark CPU score of 128,741.43. Memory bandwidth is strong, achieving 657.87 GB/sec during large-block read operations and 254.77 GB/sec on sustained writes. High-throughput data processing is further confirmed by top-tier performance in Clang compilation, ray tracing, bzip3 multi-threaded decompression at 803.1 GB/sec, and 196.23 million Redis SET operations per second.

From an infrastructure perspective, the D128lds_v7 emphasizes high compute and local I/O density over memory capacity. Its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides a lean memory baseline, making it cost-efficient for parallel tasks that fully saturate 128 compute threads without demanding expansive RAM pools. The included 7559 GB NVMe SSD eliminates the latency overhead of network-attached block devices for high-churn scratch data. The primary hardware tradeoff is the lower memory-per-core ratio, which constrains giant in-memory databases. Consequently, the instance fits compute-intensive compilation pipelines, large-scale static web serving, high-volume batch data decompression, and fast local database operations.
description: Microsoft Azure D128lds_v7 is a high-density compute server provisioned with 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores using the Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running up to 4.2 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture and Hyper-V virtualization, the instance integrates 256 GB of system RAM, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and includes 7559 GB of local NVMe SSD storage without discrete GPUs. The processor features 480 MB of L3 cache along with AVX-512 and AMX matrix instructions, which drive top-tier parallel throughput across multi-core benchmarks, code compilation, and encryption tests. Benchmark results indicate exceptional read-write memory bandwidth and leading Redis and database operation rates. The configuration balances substantial computing density against a moderate memory footprint, delivering efficient scale for workloads bounded by CPU cycles and scratch disk speed rather than expansive in-memory footprints. Azure D128lds_v7 is suited for massive software compilation, static web delivery, batch decompression, and local I/O-intensive database systems.
